Fast Food That Accepts EBT: Chains in the Restaurant Meals Program

Updated July 20, 2026Source: USDA SNAP Retailer Locator & FNA
Short answer: Many national fast food chains take EBT at locations approved for the SNAP Restaurant Meals Program, including McDonald's, Subway, Jack in the Box, Taco Bell, Carl's Jr., Burger King, KFC, Popeyes and El Pollo Loco. The catch: only specific locations in participating states (mainly California and Arizona) are authorized, and only eligible RMP recipients can use EBT there. A location accepting EBT in one city doesn't mean every branch does.

The chains people ask about most do participate in RMP — but participation is location-by-location, not company-wide. Here's the real picture.

Popular chains with RMP locations

These national chains have the most EBT-authorized restaurants in our data. Tap any to see participating locations by state and city:

  • McDonald's and Subway — the widest RMP coverage
  • Jack in the Box, Taco Bell, Carl's Jr.
  • Burger King, KFC, Popeyes
  • El Pollo Loco, Pizza Hut, Del Taco

See the full list of chains for every brand with authorized locations.

Why not every location takes EBT

Each individual restaurant has to be authorized for RMP — it's not automatic across a brand. A McDonald's in Los Angeles may accept EBT while one two towns over doesn't, and chains outside participating states don't take it at all. Always confirm the specific location, either by our listings or by asking staff.

The two conditions, every time

  1. The location is authorized — in a participating state and signed up for RMP.
  2. You're an eligible recipient — 60+, disabled, or experiencing homelessness. See who qualifies.

Frequently asked questions

Does every McDonald's take EBT?

No — only locations authorized for RMP in participating states, and only for eligible recipients. Check the specific restaurant on our McDonald's page.

What fast food takes EBT in California?

California has the most options: McDonald's, Subway, Jack in the Box, Carl's Jr., Taco Bell, Burger King and many more at authorized locations. Browse by city from the California state page.

Can I use EBT at fast food if I just have regular SNAP?

Only if you're enrolled in RMP (60+, disabled, or homeless) and in a participating state. Standard SNAP alone doesn't cover restaurant food.
